title: Integration Ops Ritual — Onboarding Sync
summary: Introductory onboarding sync to align runbook, networking, and go-live readiness for Redwood deployment in BluePelican's VPC. Covered SSO/KMS, canary rollout plan, performance baseline request, and next steps for pilot start.
topics: VPC networking requirements and IP whitelisting
SSO & SAML onboarding and RBAC mapping
Pilot scope: endpoints, SLA and traffic shaping
Benchmarks: latency/cost goals and test harness
action_items: Ethan: Share Dedicated vs Hosted pricing matrix and example commit profiles by 2026-03-25
Maya: Runbook draft (network step-by-step + firewall rules) v0.1 by 2026-03-24
Priya: Share onboarding checklist and support escalation contacts by 2026-03-23
Ana: Provide sample TLS cert chain and egress IPs from infra team by 2026-03-26
Tom: Schedule internal security review with infra and legal for week of 3/29
next_steps: Redwood to send pilot SOW template and pricing examples
Customer to provision a staging VPC and a small test dataset for perf benchmarks
Set up a canary rollout window (low traffic) week of 4/5
Follow-up technical deep dive with SE to run perf harness and token-cost estimates
transcript:
Meeting header
Date: 2026-03-22 16:00 PT
Duration: 48 minutes
Attendees: Ethan Park, Maya Lopez, Priya Singh (Redwood); Tom Keller, Ana Moreno, Jasper Li (BluePelican)
---
Summary (auto): quick kickoff style onboarding, runbook and network checklist.

[00:00:00] Ethan Park: Hey everyone, thanks for hopping on. um quick intro — I'm Ethan, AE at Redwood Inference. with me is Maya, our SE, and Priya, our CSM. how's everyone doing on your side?
[00:00:12] Tom Keller: Morning, Ethan — Tom here. doing good. we had a busy week but excited to get this moving.
[00:00:18] Jasper Li: Hi all. Jasper, CTO. hoping to keep the window short — got a security sync after.
[00:00:23] Maya Lopez: totally, we'll try to keep to the runbook and the network bits first then the pilot scope.
[00:00:29] Priya Singh: quick agenda — runbook & VPC items, SSO + RBAC mapping, pilot scope and perf goals, next steps. sound right?
[00:00:36] Ana Moreno: yep that's perfect.

[00:00:45] Ethan Park: Great. first, networking — BluePelican wants Redwood Private inside their VPC, correct? Ana, can you confirm what you currently support for egress and peering?
[00:00:58] Ana Moreno: we're planning to host in our AWS account. we can peer or we can use a managed egress. right now the security team prefers VPC peering or transit gateway rather than opening wide egress.
[00:01:10] Maya Lopez: got it. for Private deployments we support VPC peering, transit gateway, and private link options. note we also provide a small set of static egress IPs if you prefer to whitelist. those IPs are included in the runbook sample.
[00:01:25] Tom Keller: static IPs are better for us right now. fewer firewall rules. what about the KV cache and state — any special ports?
[00:01:34] Maya Lopez: no extra ports beyond standard HTTPS for the control plane and the inference endpoints. the KV cache is local to the inference nodes, nothing you need to open externally.
[00:01:45] Jasper Li: how about latency — we want sub 60ms p50 for the short completion path on the pilot model. is that realistic in our region?
[00:01:56] Maya Lopez: it's achievable depending on model choice and quantization profile. for example, using a quantized Llama-3-small variant on a dedicated GPU pool we often see p50 around 40–70 ms for short sequences. we'll need to run the perf harness on your infra to validate.
[00:02:12] Ethan Park: also tradeoff reminder — lower latency can increase cost per token, so we'll show Dedicated vs Hosted economics in the matrix.

[00:02:25] Ana Moreno: ok, good. on identity: we use Okta and will require SAML SSO + SCIM provisioning. we also have strict RBAC mapping that maps to AD groups.
[00:02:37] Priya Singh: Redwood supports SAML SSO and SCIM, and we can map groups to roles in the Console. we can share the SSO guide and a sample attribute mapping.
[00:02:48] Tom Keller: and audit logs — retention requirements are 2 years. do you provide exportable audit logs, or will we need to pull them into our SIEM?
[00:02:58] Maya Lopez: audit logs are exportable via S3 or SIEM forwarder. retention on our Private offering can be customer-configured or we can set up a push to your S3 with lifecycle rules.
[00:03:08] Jasper Li: KMS — keys need to be customer-managed. we can't have provider-managed keys for production data.
[00:03:16] Maya Lopez: understood. Private deployment integrates with customer KMS/HSM and we can point the runtime to your CMK for encryption-at-rest and TLS certs. we'll add the KMS checklist to the runbook.

[00:03:30] Ethan Park: quick note on compliance — you mentioned SOC 2 earlier in the RFP. Redwood's Private control plane package includes audit artifacts and SOC 2 attestation documents; I'll send those Docs after the call.
[00:03:42] Jasper Li: yes please — legal will want those.

[00:03:47] Ana Moreno: for the pilot, we planned three routes: 1) customer support assistant (small models), 2) internal doc search embeddings, 3) a reranking route for search. can we scope those?
[00:03:58] Maya Lopez: that's a good spread. for embeddings we can demo our high-throughput batch pipeline. for reranking we'll need to tune latency vs cost — reranking can tolerate slightly higher latency depending on your UI.
[00:04:12] Tom Keller: what about model pinning and rollouts? we need canaries for a/b testing during rollout windows.
[00:04:19] Maya Lopez: Redwood Console supports canary rollouts and traffic splits by route or model version. you can configure traffic percentages and automatic rollback on errors or quality regressions. we'll show the dashboard in the follow-up SE deep dive.

[00:04:33] Ethan Park: Let's talk timeline. Customer wants pilot in staging by 4/5, low-traffic canary week of 4/12 and production ramp after approvals. realistic?
[00:04:43] Tom Keller: 4/5 for staging sounds tight but doable if we get the runbook and VPC details today.
[00:04:49] Priya Singh: we'll prioritize the runbook steps — Maya will draft the network and SSO sections. Ethan will send the pricing matrix.

[00:04:59] Ana Moreno: one small thing — our security team will run a pentest on the Private control plane. they want to know if there are any known hardening steps we should do before that.
[00:05:10] Maya Lopez: we'll include an infra hardening checklist: minimal inbound ports, TLS ciphers, client cert validation for the admin endpoints, and SAML assertion expiry guidance.
[00:05:21] Jasper Li: also need a rollback playbook in case models regress in quality — who owns that?
[00:05:27] Priya Singh: Redwood owns the rollback mechanism in the Console, but the runbook will include the customer gating steps and approvals. we can map owners in the runbook (SE-owner for rollback validation, customer's product owner for business sign-off).

[00:05:40] Ethan Park: perfect. any blockers from your side for starting the pilot?
[00:05:44] Tom Keller: we need the SAML attribute mapping doc, the egress IP list, and the pricing examples. also our legal wants the SOC 2 paperwork.
[00:05:54] Ethan Park: we'll get all that over. action items noted.

[00:06:01] Maya Lopez: for the perf harness, we'll need a small representative dataset and a test user script. can Ana share a stripped-down sample by 3/26?
[00:06:12] Ana Moreno: yeah we can do that, I'll coordinate with infra to scrub PII and send over a 10k row sample.

[00:06:18] Jasper Li: last question — do you have any tips for token cost optimization? we saw a big delta in a previous vendor.
[00:06:24] Maya Lopez: yes — batching, prefix caching, and model quantization are the three big levers. Redwood Optimize can recommend batching sizes and a quantization profile based on the workload. we'll include a first-pass recommendation after the perf run.
[00:06:40] Tom Keller: great.

[00:06:45] Ethan Park: okay, to recap: Maya drafts runbook network + SSO; Ethan sends pricing matrix and SOC2 docs; Priya shares onboarding checklist and escalation contacts; Ana provides TLS/cert chain and sample dataset. we'll aim to have staging by 4/5.
[00:06:59] Priya Singh: I'll set up the follow-up SE deep dive for next week — slot for perf harness and Console walkthrough.

[00:07:07] Jasper Li: thanks all, gotta run to security call. appreciate the clear next steps.
[00:07:12] Ethan Park: thanks — we'll circulate notes and the runbook link.

[00:07:18] Call end (auto).
